1 // drivers/index.mjs — the pluggable model-backend registry + the single `runAgent`
2 // seam the trio engines call. One interface, swappable backends:
3 //
4 //   runAgent({ prompt, schema, freshContext, driver })
5 //
6 // The backend is selected by (in order): an explicit `driver` argument, the
7 // `TRIO_DRIVER` env var, else the default `'claude'`. Wave 4 ships only the Claude
8 // backend (the existing `claude -p` behavior, untouched — the non-regression
9 // guarantee); Wave 5 adds gemini/openai/grok by calling `registerDriver(...)`.
10 //
11 // A driver is `{ name, subAgentCapable, runAgent({ prompt, schema, freshContext }) }`.
12 // `runAgent` returns the model's text by default, or a schema-validated object when
13 // `schema` is supplied (every backend retries once, then fails honestly).

33 /**
34  * Anchor attribution sink (Wave 2 S3). When Anchor spawned the process that runs
35  * this seat, `ANCHOR_RECEIPTS_DIR` names a folder; every physical receipt that
36  * carries a receipt object is dropped there as ONE small JSON file: the ids the
37  * process inherited (project, effort dir, job, session), the seat's own session,
38  * family, served model, usage, cost. Anchor sweeps the folder through its usage
39  * seam. Best-effort: an observer must never break the seat.
40  */
41 export function sinkAnchorReceipt(driver, opts, entry, env = process.env) {
42   const dir = env?.ANCHOR_RECEIPTS_DIR;
43   const rec = entry?.receipt;
44   if (!dir || !rec || typeof rec !== 'object') return null;
45   try {
46     const body = {
47       at: new Date().toISOString().replace(/\.\d{3}Z$/, 'Z'),
48       kind: entry?.kind ?? null,
49       family: rec.model_family || requestedFamilyForDriver(driver?.name),
50       model_served: rec.model_served ?? null,
51       model_attested: rec.model_attested === true,
52       native_id: rec.thread_id ?? rec.session_id ?? null,
53       usage: rec.usage && typeof rec.usage === 'object' ? rec.usage : null,
54       cost_usd: typeof rec.cost_usd === 'number' ? rec.cost_usd
55         : typeof rec.total_cost_usd === 'number' ? rec.total_cost_usd : null,
56       duration_ms: typeof rec.duration_ms === 'number' ? rec.duration_ms : null,
57       cwd: process.cwd(),
58       env: {
59         project_id: env.ANCHOR_PROJECT_ID || null,
60         effort_dir: env.ANCHOR_EFFORT_DIR || null,
61         job_id: env.ANCHOR_JOB_ID || null,
62         session_id: env.ANCHOR_SESSION_ID || null,
63       },
64     };
65     fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
66     const file = path.join(dir, `${randomUUID()}.json`);
67     fs.writeFileSync(`${file}.part`, JSON.stringify(body));
68     fs.renameSync(`${file}.part`, file);
69     return file;
70   } catch {
71     return null;
72   }
73 }

81 /** Map a model family name (claude|gemini|grok|chatgpt) → registered trio driver name. */
82 export function familyToDriverName(family) {
83   const f = String(family || '').trim().toLowerCase();
84   if (f === 'gemini') return 'gemini-cli';
85   // Subscription Grok Build CLI (`grok -p`) — NOT the raw xAI HTTP API (`grok` driver).
86   if (f === 'grok') return 'grok-cli';
87   // Subscription Codex CLI (`codex exec`) — NOT the raw OpenAI HTTP API (`openai` driver).
88   if (f === 'chatgpt' || f === 'codex') return 'chatgpt-cli';
89   if (f === 'claude' || !f) return 'claude';
90   return null;
91 }

93 /**
94  * Read coding/review families from Anchor's durable settings/mirror only.
95  * Legacy process family variables are outputs for child compatibility, never
96  * an input that may outrank or replace the user's saved preference.
97  */
98 const VALID_MODEL_FAMILIES = new Set(['claude', 'gemini', 'grok', 'chatgpt']);
99 
100 function readPrefsFile(file) {
101   if (!file || !fs.existsSync(file)) return null;
102   let raw;
103   try {
104     raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'));
105   } catch (error) {
106     throw new HaltError(
107       `Anchor model preferences are unreadable: ${file}`,
108       `repair the JSON preference store (${error.message}); family routing will not guess`,
109     );
110   }
111   if (!raw || typeof raw !== 'object' || Array.isArray(raw)) {
112     throw new HaltError(
113       `Anchor model preferences are invalid: ${file}`,
114       'expected a JSON object; family routing will not guess',
115     );
116   }
117   for (const key of ['coding_family', 'review_family']) {
118     const value = raw[key];
119     if (value !== undefined && !VALID_MODEL_FAMILIES.has(String(value).trim().toLowerCase())) {
120       throw new HaltError(
121         `unknown ${key} "${value}" in ${file}`,
122         `expected one of ${[...VALID_MODEL_FAMILIES].join('|')}`,
123       );
124     }
125   }
126   return raw;
127 }

130   const prefs = loadPolicyPrefs(env);
131   return { coding: prefs.coding_family, review: prefs.review_family,
132     terminal: prefs.default_cli, cross_model: prefs.coding_family !== prefs.review_family,
133     source: prefs.source, settings_revision: prefs.settings_revision,
134     model_policy: prefs.model_policy };

137 /**
138  * Resolve driver name from Anchor coding/review family prefs for a role.
139  * Explicit TRIO_DRIVER / opts.driver still win over this (callers apply order).
140  * @returns {?string} registered driver name or null
141  */
142 export function resolveDriverFromFamilies(role, env = process.env) {
143   const r = normalizeRole(
144     role && typeof role === 'object' ? role : { role },
145   );
146   const fams = loadModelFamilies(env);
147   const family = isVerificationRole({ role: r }) ? fams.review : fams.coding;
148   return familyToDriverName(family);
149 }

151 /** Open a caller-held, serial, read-only structured-data session. There is no
152  * failover: unsupported family/capability is an honest refusal before any turn.
153  * Data roles use the configured coding family; canonical verification roles refuse.
154  * @returns {Promise<{pid:number, threadId:string, request:Function, cancel:Function, close:Function}>}
155  */
156 export async function createDataSession(options = {}) {
157   const env = options.env ?? process.env;
158   const role = normalizeRole(options);
159   if (isVerificationRole({ role })) {
160     throw new DataSessionError('capability_unavailable', 'Verification roles cannot use persistent data sessions');
161   }
162   if (options.capability !== undefined && options.capability !== 'read-only-data') {
163     throw new DataSessionError('capability_unavailable', 'Only read-only-data sessions are supported');
164   }
165   const driver = resolveDriverFromFamilies({ role }, env);
166   if (options.driver && options.driver !== driver) {
167     throw new DataSessionError('capability_unavailable', 'Data session driver must match the configured coding family');
168   }
169   if (driver !== 'chatgpt-cli') {
170     throw new DataSessionError('capability_unavailable', `Selected driver ${driver || 'unknown'} does not support persistent read-only data sessions`);
171   }
172   // Real production seats resolve the common latest/highest policy before
173   // spawning, then validate availability and effort against the child catalog.
174   // An injected fake process keeps its hermetic resolver seam.
175   const policy = options.spawnImpl ? {} : {
176     policyEnvironment,
177     policyResolver: (family, args) => {
178       const selection = resolveModelPolicy(family, args);
179       return { model: selection.model, effort: selection.effort, receipt: selection };
180     },
181   };
182   return openChatgptDataSession({ ...options, role, env, ...policy });
183 }

185 /**
186  * Build an explicit role→{driver} route table from coding/review family prefs.
187  * Used by live Crucible / researchPrime / Gandalf builders so seats honor the
188  * dashboard knobs (and ~/.anchor/model_prefs.json) instead of hardcoding Claude.
189  *
190  * @param {object} [o]
191  * @param {string[]} [o.codingRoles]  seats on CODING_FAMILY (plus `default`)
192  * @param {string[]} [o.reviewRoles]  seats on REVIEW_FAMILY
193  * @param {object}   [o.env]
194  * @param {?string}  [o.reviewModel]  optional model pin on every review seat
195  * @returns {{ routes: object, families: object, codingDriver: string, reviewDriver: string, drafterFamily: string, refuterFamily: string }}
196  */
197 export function buildRoutesFromFamilies({
198   codingRoles = ['synthesizer'],
199   reviewRoles = [...VERIFICATION_ROLES],
200   env = process.env,
201   reviewModel = null,
202 } = {}) {
203   const families = loadModelFamilies(env);
204   const codingDriver = familyToDriverName(families.coding) || 'claude';
205   const reviewDriver = familyToDriverName(families.review) || 'claude';
206   const routes = { default: { driver: codingDriver } };
207   for (const role of codingRoles) {
208     const r = normalizeRole({ role });
209     if (!r || r === 'default') continue;
210     routes[r] = { driver: codingDriver };
211   }
212   for (const role of reviewRoles) {
213     const r = normalizeRole({ role });
214     if (!r) continue;
215     const entry = { driver: reviewDriver };
216     routes[r] = entry;
217   }
218   return {
219     routes: Object.freeze({ ...routes }),
220     families,
221     codingDriver,
222     reviewDriver,
223     drafterFamily: families.coding,
224     refuterFamily: families.review,
225   };
226 }

228 /**
229  * Stamp TRIO_DRIVER_<ROLE> (and CODING_FAMILY / REVIEW_FAMILY) from prefs when
230  * unset — so Foreman run-live and other env-driven seats pick up dashboard knobs
231  * without a per-project models block. Never overwrites an explicit operator env.
232  * @param {object} [env=process.env]
233  * @returns {{ coding, review, cross_model }}
234  */
235 export function applyFamilyPrefsToEnv(env = process.env) {
236   const fams = loadModelFamilies(env);
237   const codingDrv = familyToDriverName(fams.coding) || 'claude';
238   const reviewDrv = familyToDriverName(fams.review) || 'claude';
239   const roleMap = {
240     EXECUTE: codingDrv,
241     FIX: codingDrv,
242     SYNTHESIZER: codingDrv,
243     DEFAULT: codingDrv,
244     REVIEW: reviewDrv,
245     SHARK: reviewDrv,
246     REVIEWER: reviewDrv,
247     JUDGE: reviewDrv,
248     DEBATE: reviewDrv,
249     REFUTER: reviewDrv,
250     GATE3: reviewDrv,
251     VERIFY: reviewDrv,
252     ATTACKER: reviewDrv,
253     ANALYSIS: reviewDrv,
254   };
255   // Always stamp from Anchor prefs (overwrite stale setx TRIO_DRIVER_* pins).
256   for (const [R, drv] of Object.entries(roleMap)) {
257     env[`TRIO_DRIVER_${R}`] = drv;
258   }
259   env.CODING_FAMILY = fams.coding;
260   env.REVIEW_FAMILY = fams.review;
261   env.CROSS_MODEL = fams.cross_model ? 'true' : 'false';
262   return fams;
263 }

266 const REGISTRY = new Map([[claudeDriver.name, claudeDriver]]);

268 /**
269  * Register (or replace) a backend. Wave 5's gemini/openai/grok modules call this.
270  * @param {{name:string, subAgentCapable?:boolean, runAgent:Function}} driver
271  */
272 export function registerDriver(driver) {
273   if (!driver || typeof driver.name !== 'string' || typeof driver.runAgent !== 'function') {
274     throw new TypeError('registerDriver requires a { name, runAgent } driver object');
275   }
276   REGISTRY.set(driver.name, driver);
277   return driver;
278 }

280 // Wave 5: register the additive non-Claude backends. They live behind the same
281 // `runAgent` interface and are selected by `TRIO_DRIVER` (the Claude default is
282 // unaffected). Registering here (rather than self-registering on import) keeps the
283 // registry's contents explicit and order-stable for the capability matrix.
284 // `gemini-cli` is the sub-agent-capable Gemini HOST backend (login-based `gemini -p`);
285 // `gemini` remains the raw-HTTP API worker. Both register; they never collide on name.
286 registerDriver(geminiCliDriver);
287 registerDriver(geminiDriver);
288 registerDriver(openaiDriver);
289 registerDriver(grokDriver); // optional API-key HTTP backend (name: 'grok')
290 registerDriver(grokCliDriver); // subscription CLI backend (name: 'grok-cli') — coding/review family default
291 registerDriver(chatgptCliDriver); // subscription Codex CLI (name: 'chatgpt-cli') — ChatGPT login, never OPENAI_API_KEY
292 
293 /** The backend names currently registered (default `claude` always present). */
294 export function listDrivers() {
295   return [...REGISTRY.keys()];
296 }

298 /**
299  * The capability matrix: one row per registered backend describing whether it can
300  * spawn real fresh sub-agent contexts (`subAgentCapable` — true only for the
301  * CLI-spawning Claude backend; the raw-API backends approximate isolation with a
302  * fresh stateless request) and HOW it produces structured output (CLI sub-agent
303  * prompt vs JSON-mode / function-calling). Derived from the registered drivers so
304  * a newly registered backend appears automatically.
305  * @returns {{name:string, subAgentCapable:boolean, structuredOutput:string}[]}
306  */
307 export function capabilityMatrix() {
308   return [...REGISTRY.values()].map((d) => ({
309     name: d.name,
310     subAgentCapable: !!d.subAgentCapable,
311     structuredOutput: d.structuredOutput ?? 'unknown',
312   }));
313 }

315 /**
316  * Resolve the active backend. Selection order: explicit `name` arg, then
317  * `TRIO_DRIVER`, then the `claude` default. HALTs on an unknown name rather than
318  * silently falling back, so a typo never quietly bills the wrong backend.
319  * @param {?string} [name]
320  * @param {object}  [env=process.env]
321  */
322 export function getDriver(name = null, env = process.env) {
323   const key = name || env.TRIO_DRIVER || DEFAULT_DRIVER;
324   const driver = REGISTRY.get(key);
325   if (!driver) {
326     throw new HaltError(
327       `unknown trio driver "${key}"`,
328       `registered drivers: ${listDrivers().join(', ')}. Set TRIO_DRIVER to one of these (or leave it unset for the default "${DEFAULT_DRIVER}").`,
329     );
330   }
331   return driver;
332 }

334 const RECEIPT_FAMILIES = new Set(['claude', 'gemini', 'grok', 'chatgpt']);
335 
336 function bounded(value, fallback = '', max = 240) {
337   const clean = String(value ?? '').replace(/[\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/g, ' ').trim();
338   return (clean || fallback).slice(0, max);
339 }
340 
341 function errorInfo(code, message = '') {
342   return {
343     code: bounded(code, 'seat_unavailable'),
344     message: bounded(message, '', 500),
345   };
346 }
347 
348 function requestedFamilyForDriver(name) {
349   const driverName = String(name || '').trim().toLowerCase();
350   if (driverName === 'claude') return 'claude';
351   if (driverName === 'gemini' || driverName.startsWith('gemini-cli')) return 'gemini';
352   if (driverName === 'grok' || driverName === 'grok-cli') return 'grok';
353   if (driverName === 'openai' || driverName === 'chatgpt-cli') return 'chatgpt';
354   return 'unknown';
355 }
356 
357 function requestedFor(driver, opts, entries = []) {
358   const rawRequested = entries
359     .map((entry) => entry?.receipt?.requested_model)
360     .find((value) => typeof value === 'string' && value.trim());
361   const explicit = typeof opts.model === 'string' && opts.model.trim() ? opts.model : null;
362   return {
363     driver: bounded(driver.name, 'unknown-driver'),
364     family: requestedFamilyForDriver(driver.name),
365     model: bounded(rawRequested ?? explicit, '', 240) || null,
366   };
367 }

369 function servedFromRaw(raw, driverName, { accepted = false } = {}) {
370   if (!raw || typeof raw !== 'object') return null;
371   const nested = raw.served && typeof raw.served === 'object' ? raw.served : null;
372   const familyValue = nested?.family ?? raw.model_family ?? null;
373   const normalizedFamily = typeof familyValue === 'string'
374     ? familyValue.trim().toLowerCase()
375     : null;
376   const familyAttested = (nested?.family_attested === true || raw.family_attested === true)
377     && RECEIPT_FAMILIES.has(normalizedFamily);
378   const modelValue = nested?.model ?? raw.model_served ?? null;
379   const normalizedModel = typeof modelValue === 'string' && modelValue.trim()
380     ? modelValue.trim().slice(0, 240)
381     : null;
382   const modelAttested = (nested?.model_attested === true || raw.model_attested === true)
383     && normalizedModel !== null;
384   if (!accepted && !familyAttested && !modelAttested) return null;
385   return {
386     driver: bounded(nested?.driver ?? driverName, 'unknown-driver'),
387     family: familyAttested ? normalizedFamily : null,
388     model: modelAttested ? normalizedModel : null,
389     family_attested: familyAttested,
390     model_attested: modelAttested,
391   };
392 }
393 
394 function normalizeTransportEntry(entry, ordinal, driverName, fallbackLabel) {
395   const raw = entry?.receipt && typeof entry.receipt === 'object' ? entry.receipt : null;
396   const kind = ordinal === 2 ? 'schema_reprompt' : 'initial';
397   const label = bounded(entry?.label ?? raw?.label, fallbackLabel || '(unlabeled)');
398   let status = entry?.outcome;
399   if (!['accepted', 'schema_rejected', 'seat_unavailable', 'aborted'].includes(status)) {
400     status = raw?.status === 'aborted' || raw?.aborted === true
401       ? 'aborted'
402       : raw?.ok === true
403         ? 'accepted'
404         : 'seat_unavailable';
405   }
406   if (!raw) status = 'seat_unavailable';
407   if (raw && raw.ok !== true && (status === 'accepted' || status === 'schema_rejected')) {
408     status = raw.status === 'aborted' || raw.aborted === true ? 'aborted' : 'seat_unavailable';
409   }
410   const acceptedProvider = raw?.ok === true;
411   const served = servedFromRaw(raw, driverName, {
412     accepted: acceptedProvider && (status === 'accepted' || status === 'schema_rejected'),
413   });
414   let error = null;
415   if (status === 'schema_rejected') {
416     error = errorInfo('schema_nonconforming', entry?.error || 'provider reply did not conform to the requested schema');
417   } else if (status === 'aborted') {
418     error = errorInfo('aborted', raw?.error || entry?.error || 'transport aborted');
419   } else if (status === 'seat_unavailable') {
420     const code = raw ? (raw.status || 'seat_unavailable') : 'missing_raw_receipt';
421     error = errorInfo(code, raw?.error || entry?.error || (raw
422       ? 'provider transport did not complete successfully'
423       : 'driver returned or threw without a physical transport receipt'));
424   }
425   return {
426     ordinal,
427     kind,
428     label,
429     ok: status === 'accepted',
430     status,
431     provider_status: raw?.kill_status === 'kill_failed'
432       ? 'kill_failed'
433       : raw?.status != null
434         ? bounded(raw.status, '', 240) || null
435         : null,
436     served,
437     error,
438   };
439 }

441 const PHYSICAL_OUTCOMES = new Set([
442   'accepted', 'schema_rejected', 'seat_unavailable', 'aborted',
443 ]);
444 
445 function physicalSequenceError(entries, count) {
446   if (count > 2) return `driver reported ${count} physical attempts; maximum is two`;
447   for (const [index, entry] of entries.entries()) {
448     if (!entry || typeof entry !== 'object' || !PHYSICAL_OUTCOMES.has(entry.outcome)) {
449       return `physical attempt ${index + 1} has an invalid outcome`;
450     }
451   }
452   if (entries[0]?.kind !== 'initial') return 'first physical attempt must be initial';
453   if (entries.length === 2) {
454     if (entries[0].outcome !== 'schema_rejected') {
455       return 'a second physical attempt requires an initial schema_rejected outcome';
456     }
457     if (entries[1].kind !== 'schema_reprompt') {
458       return 'second physical attempt must be schema_reprompt';
459     }
460   }
461   return null;
462 }
463 
464 async function runDispatcherAttempt(driver, opts, ordinal, kind) {
465   const entries = [];
466   let physicalCount = 0;
467   let usedPhysicalHook = false;
468   let value;
469   let thrown = null;
470   if (opts.signal?.aborted) {
471     entries.push({
472       outcome: 'aborted', label: opts.label,
473       receipt: { ok: false, status: 'aborted', aborted: true, error: 'seat aborted before spawn' },
474     });
475     thrown = Object.assign(new Error('seat aborted before spawn'), { aborted: true });
476   } else {
477     try {
478       value = await driver.runAgent({
479         ...opts,
480         onReceipt: undefined,
481         [PHYSICAL_RECEIPT_HOOK]: (entry) => {
482           usedPhysicalHook = true;
483           physicalCount += 1;
484           if (entries.length < 2) entries.push(entry);
485           // Tee to a caller-supplied hook: the public trio.seat.v1 receipt keeps its
486           // exact-key shape (strict consumers validate it), so measured usage on the
487           // raw physical receipt is only reachable through this opt-in channel.
488           const callerHook = opts[PHYSICAL_RECEIPT_HOOK];
489           if (typeof callerHook === 'function') {
490             try { callerHook(entry); } catch { /* observer must never break the seat */ }
491           }
492           sinkAnchorReceipt(driver, opts, entry);
493         },
494       });
495     } catch (error) {
496       thrown = error;
497       if (entries.length === 0 && error?.raw_receipt) {
498         entries.push({ receipt: error.raw_receipt, label: opts.label });
499       }
500     }
501   }
502   const contractError = usedPhysicalHook
503     ? physicalSequenceError(entries, physicalCount)
504     : null;
505   if (entries.length === 0) {
506     entries.push({ receipt: null, label: opts.label, error: thrown?.message });
507   }
508   const requested = requestedFor(driver, opts, contractError ? [] : entries);
509   const transportAttempts = contractError
510     ? [{
511       ordinal: 1,
512       kind: 'initial',
513       label: bounded(opts.label, '(unlabeled)'),
514       ok: false,
515       status: 'seat_unavailable',
516       provider_status: null,
517       served: null,
518       error: errorInfo('invalid_physical_receipt_sequence', contractError),
519     }]
520     : entries.map((entry, index) => normalizeTransportEntry(
521       entry,
522       index + 1,
523       driver.name,
524       index === 0 ? opts.label : `${opts.label}#retry`,
525     ));
526   const last = transportAttempts.at(-1);
527   const verification = isVerificationRole({ role: opts.role, label: opts.label });
528   let status;
529   let served = null;
530   let error = null;
531   if (contractError) {
532     status = 'seat_unavailable';
533     error = errorInfo('invalid_physical_receipt_sequence', contractError);
534   } else if (thrown?.aborted || last.status === 'aborted') {
535     status = 'aborted';
536     error = errorInfo('aborted', thrown?.message || last.error?.message || 'transport aborted');
537   } else if (thrown) {
538     status = transportAttempts.length === 2
539       && transportAttempts.every((attempt) => attempt.status === 'schema_rejected')
540       ? 'schema_exhausted'
541       : 'seat_unavailable';
542     error = errorInfo(
543       status === 'schema_exhausted' ? 'schema_nonconforming' : (thrown.seat_status || 'seat_unavailable'),
544       thrown.message,
545     );
546   } else if (last.status !== 'accepted') {
547     status = transportAttempts.length === 2
548       && transportAttempts.every((attempt) => attempt.status === 'schema_rejected')
549       ? 'schema_exhausted'
550       : last.status === 'aborted'
551         ? 'aborted'
552         : 'seat_unavailable';
553     error = errorInfo(last.error?.code || 'seat_unavailable', last.error?.message || 'transport failed');
554   } else if (verification && !last.served?.family_attested) {
555     status = 'seat_unavailable';
556     error = errorInfo('served_unattested', 'verification requires an attested served family');
557   } else {
558     // (John, 2026-09-05) a verification seat whose FAMILY is attested but whose served MODEL
559     // is not (the Codex CLI names no model; Grok plain output did not) is ACCEPTED with the
560     // honest stamp `model_attested:false` on its receipt — family independence is what a
561     // reviewer must prove; the model tier is stamped, never inferred. Said on the log so no
562     // run is blind to it. A family that cannot be attested still fails closed above.
563     if (verification && !last.served?.model_attested) {
564       const say = typeof opts.log === 'function' ? opts.log : () => {};
565       say(`⚠ ${opts.label ?? opts.role ?? 'seat'}: ${driver.name} verification seat served family "${last.served?.family ?? '?'}" with an UNATTESTED model — accepted, stamped model_attested:false`);
566     }
567     status = transportAttempts.length === 2 ? 'success_after_schema_reprompt' : 'success';
568     served = last.served;
569   }
570   const ok = status === 'success' || status === 'success_after_schema_reprompt';
571   return {
572     value,
573     replay_safe: !contractError && entries.length === 1 && entries[0]?.receipt?.replay_safe === true,
574     attempt: {
575       ordinal,
576       kind,
577       requested,
578       ok,
579       status,
580       served: ok ? served : null,
581       transport_attempts: transportAttempts,
582       error: ok ? null : error,
583     },
584   };
585 }
586 
587 export class ReceiptCallbackError extends Error {
588   constructor(cause, receipt) {
589     super(`Trio receipt callback failed: ${cause?.message ?? cause}`);
590     this.name = 'ReceiptCallbackError';
591     this.cause = cause;
592     this.receipt = receipt;
593   }
594 }
595 
596 function failedSeatError(receipt) {
597   const error = new HaltError(
598     `trio seat ${receipt.status}: ${receipt.label}`,
599     receipt.error?.message || 'inspect the attached trio.seat.v1 receipt',
600   );
601   error.receipt = receipt;
602   error.aborted = receipt.status === 'aborted';
603   if (!error.aborted) error.seat_unavailable = true;
604   error.seat_status = receipt.status;
605   error.requested_model = receipt.requested.model;
606   error.served_model = null;
607   return error;
608 }
609 
610 function finalizeReceipt({ opts, role, verification, requested, attempts, status, served, error }) {
611   return {
612     schema: 'trio.seat.v1',
613     ok: status === 'success' || status === 'success_after_failover',
614     status,
615     label: bounded(opts.label, role || requested.driver || '(unlabeled)'),
616     role,
617     verification,
618     structured: !!opts.schema,
619     requested,
620     served,
621     attempts,
622     failover: {
623       allowed: !verification,
624       used: attempts.length > 1,
625       blocked_reason: verification
626         ? 'verification_seat'
627         : status === 'seat_unavailable' && attempts.length === 1
628           ? 'no_capable_fallback'
629           : null,
630     },
631     error,
632   };
633 }
634 
635 /**
636  * The single engine seam. Dispatches to the selected backend's `runAgent`.
637  * @param {object}  opts
638  * @param {string}  opts.prompt
639  * @param {object}  [opts.schema]        JSON Schema; when present the reply is parsed/validated
640  * @param {boolean} [opts.freshContext]  request an isolated context (native for sub-agent-capable backends)
641  * @param {string}  [opts.driver]        explicit backend name (overrides TRIO_DRIVER)
642  * @param {string}  [opts.role]          explicit seat role; wins over label derivation
643  * @param {string}  [opts.label]         bounded diagnostic label and role fallback
644  * @param {string}  [opts.model]         requested model identity (never a served assertion)
645  * @param {AbortSignal} [opts.signal]    supervisor cancellation signal
646  * @param {Function} [opts.onReceipt]    awaited once with the successful final trio.seat.v1 receipt
647  * @returns {Promise<any>} model text, or the schema-validated object
648  */
649 export async function runAgent(opts = {}) {
650   // Driver selection order (2026-07-22 — Anchor prefs are universal source of truth):
651   //   1. explicit opts.driver (per-call pin)
652   //   2. Anchor settings.json / ~/.anchor/model_prefs.json by role
653   //   3. TRIO_DRIVER_<ROLE> (legacy setx — only if prefs did not resolve)
654   //   4. TRIO_DRIVER / default claude
655   // Stale TRIO_DRIVER_SHARK=gemini-cli setx must NOT outrank Anchor coding/review knobs.
656   // Same-family coding+review is allowed; stamp cross_model from loadModelFamilies().
657   let name = opts.driver;
658   // Hermeticity guard (2026-07-25): an injected stub transport pins the matching
659   // backend. Host model-prefs (~/.anchor/model_prefs.json) must NEVER re-route a
660   // stubbed call to a live CLI — observed: driver-interface tests spawning real
661   // billable sessions when prefs resolved coding=grok (usage-leak class, 07-14).
662   if (!name) {
663     if (opts.runClaude) name = 'claude';
664     else if (opts.runGemini) name = 'gemini-cli';
665     else if (opts.runGrokCli) name = 'grok-cli';
666     else if (opts.runCodexCli) name = 'chatgpt-cli';
667   }
668   const activeEnv = opts.env ?? process.env;
669   const role = normalizeRole({ role: opts.role, label: opts.label });
670   // Explicit test/host stores must be valid even when a stub owns transport;
671   // validation does not reroute that stub or discover a live capability.
672   if (activeEnv.ANCHOR_DATA_DIR) loadPolicyPrefs(activeEnv);
673   const injected = !!(opts.runClaude || opts.runGemini || opts.runGrokCli || opts.runCodexCli);
674   if (!injected && (!name || ['claude', 'grok-cli', 'chatgpt-cli', 'gemini-cli', 'grok', 'openai', 'gemini'].includes(name))) {
675     name = resolveDriverFromFamilies({ role, label: opts.label }, activeEnv);
676   }
677   if (!name) {
678     name = resolveDriverFromFamilies({ role, label: opts.label }, activeEnv) || null;
679   }
680   if (!name && role) {
681     const key = `TRIO_DRIVER_${role.toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z0-9]+/g, '_')}`;
682     name = activeEnv[key] || null;
683   }
684   const driver = getDriver(name, activeEnv);
685   return dispatchWithFailover(driver, { ...opts, role });
686 }
687 
688 /**
689  * Dispatch to a backend, applying the universal MODEL-INTEGRITY FAILOVER (John 2026-07-17):
690  * a NON-Claude seat that cannot deliver its ATTESTED requested model — silently substituted to a
691  * fallback (e.g. GPT-OSS, how a rate-limited OR auth-degraded agy manifests) or a transport
692  * failure — fails OVER to Claude ONE-NOTCH-BELOW-FRONTIER, honestly single-family
693  * (`cross_model:false`), with a loud flag, rather than running the seat BLIND on the wrong model.
694  * Used by BOTH `runAgent` AND `makeRoleRoutedAgent`, so EVERY trio+foundry call path inherits it.
695  * A Claude seat has nowhere better to fail over to, so it re-throws.
696  */
697 function injectedTransportFor(name, opts) {
698   return { claude: opts.runClaude, 'grok-cli': opts.runGrokCli,
699     'chatgpt-cli': opts.runCodexCli, 'gemini-cli': opts.runGemini }[name];
700 }
701 
702 async function journalRouting(opts, event) {
703   const entry = { schema: 'trio.model-routing.v1', at: new Date().toISOString(),
704     label: bounded(opts.label, opts.role || 'seat'), ...event };
705   if (typeof opts.onRoutingEvent === 'function') {
706     await opts.onRoutingEvent(entry);
707     return;
708   }
709   const env = opts.env ?? process.env;
710   const profile = env.USERPROFILE || env.HOME;
711   if (!profile) throw new HaltError('Cannot journal model failover', 'configure a private profile or onRoutingEvent journal sink');
712   const directory = path.join(profile, '.anchor', 'journal', 'runs');
713   fs.mkdirSync(directory, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
714   fs.appendFileSync(path.join(directory, 'model-routing.jsonl'), JSON.stringify(entry) + '\n', { mode: 0o600 });
715 }
716 
717 async function dispatchWithFailover(driver, opts) {
718   const role = normalizeRole({ role: opts.role, label: opts.label });
719   const verification = isVerificationRole({ role, label: opts.label });
720   const injected = !!(opts.runClaude || opts.runGemini || opts.runGrokCli || opts.runCodexCli);
721   const primary = await runDispatcherAttempt(driver, { ...opts, role }, 1, 'primary');
722   const attempts = [primary.attempt];
723   let current = primary;
724   let finalValue = primary.value;
725   let status = primary.attempt.ok ? 'success' : 'seat_unavailable';
726   let served = primary.attempt.served;
727   let topError = primary.attempt.error;
728   if (!primary.attempt.ok) {
729     if (primary.attempt.status === 'aborted' || opts.signal?.aborted) {
730       status = 'aborted';
731     } else if (verification) {
732       status = 'verification_fail_closed';
733     } else if (primary.replay_safe) {
734       // Only dashboard-selected families; executable presence grants no authority.
735       const prefs = loadModelFamilies(opts.env ?? process.env);
736       const ladder = [...new Set([prefs.coding, prefs.review, prefs.terminal].map(familyToDriverName))]
737         .filter(name => name && name !== driver.name);
738       const log = typeof opts.log === 'function' ? opts.log : () => {};
739       for (const name of ladder) {
740         if (opts.signal?.aborted) { status = 'aborted'; break; }
741         if (injected && !injectedTransportFor(name, opts)) continue; // hermetic seats never escape to a real CLI
742         const event = { action: 'failover', from: current.attempt.requested.driver,
743           to: name, reason: current.attempt.error?.code || 'seat_unavailable',
744           cross_model: false, settings_revision: prefs.settings_revision };
745         await journalRouting(opts, event); // durable BEFORE launching another seat
746         log('MODEL FAILOVER: ' + event.from + ' -> ' + name + ' (' + event.reason + '; cross_model:false). Journaled.');
747         current = await runDispatcherAttempt(getDriver(name, opts.env ?? process.env), {
748           ...opts, role, driver: name, model: null, cross_model: false,
749         }, attempts.length + 1, 'fallback');
750         attempts.push(current.attempt);
751         finalValue = current.value;
752         topError = current.attempt.error;
753         if (current.attempt.ok) {
754           status = 'success_after_failover'; served = current.attempt.served; topError = null; break;
755         }
756         if (current.attempt.status === 'aborted') { status = 'aborted'; break; }
757         if (!current.replay_safe) break; // never replay uncertain work
758       }
759     }
760   }
761   if (!primary.attempt.ok && status !== 'success_after_failover') {
762     await journalRouting(opts, { action: 'halt', driver: current.attempt.requested.driver,
763       reason: topError?.code || status, verification, replay_safe: current.replay_safe });
764   }
765   const receipt = finalizeReceipt({
766     opts, role, verification, requested: primary.attempt.requested,
767     attempts, status, served: status.startsWith('success') ? served : null, error: topError,
768   });
769   if (!receipt.ok) throw failedSeatError(receipt);
770   if (typeof opts.onReceipt === 'function') {
771     try { await opts.onReceipt(receipt); }
772     catch (error) { throw new ReceiptCallbackError(error, receipt); }
773   }
774   return finalValue;
775 }
776 
777 /**
778  * Build a role-routed `agent(prompt, opts)` — the single missing primitive for mixed
779  * per-role model routing (2026-07): dispatch each call to a backend+model chosen by
780  * its role (from `opts.role`, else the label prefix before ':' / '#' / '.').
781  *
782  *   makeRoleRoutedAgent({ routes: {
783  *     synthesizer: { driver: 'claude',     model: 'claude-fable-5' },
784  *     judge:       { driver: 'claude',     model: 'claude-fable-5' },
785  *     review:      { driver: 'gemini-cli', model: 'gemini-3.1-pro' },
786  *     default:     { driver: 'claude' },
787  *   }})
788  *
789  * Unrouted roles fall to `routes.default`, else the registry default. Extra opts
790  * (env/target/log/runClaude stubs) thread through to the backend's runAgent.
791  * @param {object} [o]
792  * @param {Object<string,{driver?:string,model?:string}>} [o.routes]
793  * @returns {(prompt:string, opts?:object)=>Promise<any>}
794  */
795 export function makeRoleRoutedAgent({ routes = {}, ...baseOpts } = {}) {
796   return (prompt, o = {}) => {
797     const role = normalizeRole({ role: o.role, label: o.label });
798     const roleRoute = routes[role] || null;
799     // A generic coding default may never capture a canonical verification seat.
800     const route = roleRoute || (isVerificationRole({ role }) ? {} : (routes.default || {}));
801     // Prefs-first: coding/review family (Anchor) wins unless the route table was
802     // deliberately prefs-built (route.driver matches family) or caller pins model only.
803     // Explicit empty routes {} → pure prefs. Explicit routes with drivers (tests / same-family
804     // tables) still honor route.driver when present.
805     const activeEnv = baseOpts.env ?? process.env;
806     const fromFamily = resolveDriverFromFamilies({ role, label: o.label }, activeEnv);
807     return runAgent({
808       ...baseOpts,
809       prompt,
810       driver: roleRoute?.driver || (isVerificationRole({ role })
811         ? fromFamily
812         : (route.driver || fromFamily)) || null,
813       schema: o.schema,
814       label: o.label,
815       role,
816       model: o.model ?? route.model ?? null,
817       freshContext: true,
818       timeoutMs: o.timeoutMs ?? baseOpts.timeoutMs,
819       sandbox: o.sandbox ?? baseOpts.sandbox,
820       reasoningEffort: o.reasoningEffort ?? baseOpts.reasoningEffort,
821       orchestrationMode: o.orchestrationMode ?? baseOpts.orchestrationMode,
822       onReceipt: o.onReceipt ?? baseOpts.onReceipt,
823       signal: o.signal ?? baseOpts.signal,
824     });
825   };
826 }
827 
828 /**
829  * Build Foreman's `{ execute, review, fix }` driver routed through the registry —
830  * i.e. the foreman driver seam on top of the selected backend (default `claude`).
831  * Foreman's `makeAgentDriver` already wraps an injected `agent()`; this is the
832  * registry-level way to obtain that seam so the foreman build path goes through the
833  * driver registry rather than calling `makeAgentDriver` directly.
834  *
835  * Two modes:
836  *   - inject `agent`  — route an existing, already-instrumented `agent()` through
837  *     the seam unchanged (used by `run-live.mjs`, whose live `claude -p` transport
838  *     carries bespoke status logging that must stay byte-for-byte equivalent).
839  *   - omit `agent`    — build the agent from the registry-selected backend, so
840  *     `TRIO_DRIVER` (or an explicit `driver`) chooses the model the build sub-agents
841  *     run on. Extra opts (e.g. an injected `runClaude` stub, `env`, `target`, `log`)
842  *     thread through to the backend's `runAgent`.
843  * @param {object}   [opts]
844  * @param {string}   [opts.driver]      explicit backend name (overrides TRIO_DRIVER)
845  * @param {Function} [opts.agent]       pre-built `agent(prompt, opts)` to route as-is
846  * @param {object|false} [opts.reliability]  Wave-1 reliability-wrapper opts, or `false` to opt out
847  * @returns {Promise<{execute:Function, review:Function, fix:Function}>}
848  */
849 export async function makeForemanDriver({ driver, agent, reliability, ...opts } = {}) {
850   const { makeAgentDriver } = await import('../foreman/bin/wave-workflow.js');
851   let seamAgent = agent;
852   // Provider key for the Wave-2 per-provider breaker: the selected backend's name when
853   // we build the seam, else 'injected' for an already-instrumented agent. A sick backend
854   // is then degraded under its OWN bucket, never globally.
855   let providerName = 'injected';
856   if (!seamAgent) {
857     const backend = getDriver(driver);
858     providerName = backend.name;
859     // Forward role + model to the backend so the per-role model tier (e.g.
860     // TRIO_MODEL_<ROLE>/TRIO_DRIVER_<ROLE>, resolved in the driver ladder) is actually
861     // reachable on the Foreman build path. A DESIGNATED role/model on makeForemanDriver
862     // (its own `opts`) WINS over the per-call wave step (`o`): when a caller builds a
863     // Foreman driver pinned to a seat — e.g. { driver, role:'judge', model:'m' } — that
864     // designation must reach the backend, not be shadowed by the wave step's own
865     // 'execute'/'review'/'fix' role. Only when no designation is set does the per-call
866     // value flow through (the normal Foreman build path passes neither, so wave-step
867     // role/model behave exactly as before). Backends that ignore role/model (e.g. the
868     // Claude session-default driver) are unaffected either way.
869     seamAgent = (prompt, o = {}) => runAgent({
870       ...opts,
871       prompt,
872       driver: backend.name,
873       schema: o.schema,
874       label: o.label,
875       role: opts.role ?? o.role,
876       model: opts.model ?? o.model,
877       timeoutMs: o.timeoutMs ?? opts.timeoutMs,
878       onReceipt: o.onReceipt ?? opts.onReceipt,
879       signal: o.signal ?? opts.signal,
880       freshContext: true,
881     });
882   }
883   // Wave 1: apply the reliability wrapper at THIS agent-injection boundary (both the
884   // injected-agent and built-backend modes), so the Foreman build path gets typed
885   // retry + round-aware idempotency. Transparent on the success path; pass
886   // `reliability:false` to opt out.
887   //
888   // Wave 2: default a LIGHT per-provider breaker (keyed by the backend name) on so a
889   // sick provider degrades for the session instead of being hammered — still inert
890   // until N consecutive recoverable failures, so a healthy build is unaffected. The
891   // idle sliver + anti-laundering telemetry stay opt-in via the `reliability` config
892   // (live wiring of stdout-heartbeat / a telemetry sink is the runner's job). Any of
893   // these can be overridden — or the breaker disabled with `reliability:{breaker:false}`.
894   const reliableSeam = reliability === false
895     ? seamAgent
896     : makeReliableAgent({ agent: seamAgent, provider: providerName, breaker: {}, ...(reliability || {}) });
897   return makeAgentDriver({ agent: reliableSeam });
898 }

900 export { claudeDriver, geminiCliDriver, geminiDriver, openaiDriver, grokDriver };
